headline: Satya Nadella warns companies are paying twice for AI by revealing proprietary data
summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella states that businesses unknowingly hand over valuable data when using AI models, effectively paying twice for the service.
details: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has issued a stark warning to companies utilizing AI models. He argues that businesses are effectively paying twice for AI services: once with money for token usage, and again by unknowingly revealing proprietary knowledge that makes the AI useful.

Nadella explains that as companies feed more data into AI models to improve their performance, they are teaching the models the nuances of their businesses. This 'institutional know-how,' derived from prompts, agent tools, and corrections, is valuable data that competitors could not otherwise obtain.

He criticizes the current model where AI providers freely scrape public data for training but impose restrictive terms on customers wanting to 'distill' or study those models in return. Nadella finds this stance hypocritical, especially when providers reserve the right to learn from customer usage and interaction data.

To address this, Nadella suggests companies should 'retain ownership' of their data, including prompts and feedback. He urges them to build 'proprietary learning environments' on cloud platforms and implement 'orchestration layers' to easily switch between different AI models, avoiding vendor lock-in.

This shift is already being observed in the industry, with companies moving towards open-source AI models that can be run on-premises. This offers a more cost-effective solution and greater control over data, with some enterprises reportedly achieving nearly 90% of the performance of proprietary models at a significantly lower cost.
caption:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella warns companies are unknowingly paying twice for AI services by feeding proprietary data into models.

Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has issued a stark warning to companies utilizing AI models. He argues that businesses are effectively paying twice for AI services: once with money for token usage, and again by unknowingly revealing proprietary knowledge that makes the AI useful.

Nadella explains that as companies feed more data into AI models to improve their performance, they are teaching the models the nuances of their businesses. This 'institutional know-how,' derived from prompts, agent tools, and corrections, is valuable data that competitors could not otherwise obtain.

He criticizes the current model where AI providers freely scrape public data for training but impose restrictive terms on customers wanting to 'distill' or study those models in return. Nadella finds this stance hypocritical, especially when providers reserve the right to learn from customer usage and interaction data.

To address this, Nadella suggests companies should 'retain ownership' of their data, including prompts and feedback. He urges them to build 'proprietary learning environments' on cloud platforms and implement 'orchestration layers' to easily switch between different AI models, avoiding vendor lock-in.

This shift is already being observed in the industry, with companies moving towards open-source AI models that can be run on-premises. This offers a more cost-effective solution and greater control over data, with some enterprises reportedly achieving nearly 90% of the performance of proprietary models at a significantly lower cost.
